content_metadata.description: A physics educational video explaining the concept of interatomic spring constant and its application in materials science.

activities.description: Drawing and writing on the whiteboard

characterInteraction.description: The professor is the sole speaker, addressing the viewer directly.

scenes.contextualRelevance: The scene focuses on explaining the concept of interatomic spring constant and its relationship to macroscopic properties of materials.

mood.description: Educational and neutral with a focus on teaching.

narrativeProgression.description: The professor introduces a homework problem about interatomic spring constant.
The professor starts drawing a wire on the whiteboard and representing it as a collection of atoms.
The professor explains how adding a mass to the end of the wire stretches it.
The professor introduces the concept of spring constant.
The professor relates the wire to a system of springs in series and parallel.
The professor explains how to relate the overall spring constant of the wire to the interatomic spring constant.
The professor derives an equation for the interatomic spring constant.
The professor realizes he made a mistake in the equation and corrects it.

scenes.title: Explaining Interatomic Spring Constant

climax.description: The professor realizes he made a mistake in the equation and corrects it.
